hook: Spike Lee turned *Fort Greene* into a movie *block party*.
dek: Playback: The Brooklyn Watch Party is at BAM this weekend, with classic films, big-name curators and a free street party Saturday.

slides.label: What it is
slides.text: *Playback: The Brooklyn Watch Party*, a new festival at *BAM* in Fort Greene, *November 6 and 7*. Presented with *Spike Lee* and *Clara Wu Tsai*.

slides.label: It opened with
slides.text: *Crooklyn*, Spike Lee's love letter to 1970s Bed-Stuy, with Lee there to introduce it.

slides.label: Saturday's films
slides.text: *Love & Basketball. City of God. The Battle of Algiers. The King of Comedy. Soul to Soul.* Plus Salaam Bombay! and Divorce Italian Style.

slides.label: The curators
slides.text: *Questlove, Bryan Stevenson and John Turturro* are among the guest curators.

slides.label: The free part
slides.text: Saturday, *11 a.m. to 5 p.m.*: a *free street party* outside BAM Rose Cinemas with Brooklyn artists, music and food.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Stories from every corner of the culture, shown in the borough that made so many of its own. *Go watch a movie with a room full of people.*

question: What film would you program for a Brooklyn block party?

caption_instagram:
Playback: The Brooklyn Watch Party is at BAM in Fort Greene this weekend, presented with Spike Lee and Clara Wu Tsai. 🎬

It opened with Crooklyn. Today's slate includes Love & Basketball, City of God, The Battle of Algiers, The King of Comedy and Soul to Soul, with Questlove, Bryan Stevenson and John Turturro among the guest curators.

The free part: a street party outside BAM Rose Cinemas today, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., with Brooklyn artists, music and food. No ticket needed.

Our take: go watch a movie with a room full of people who love it as much as you do.

caption_linkedin:
A new film festival in Brooklyn is a smart model for community-first programming.

Playback: The Brooklyn Watch Party at BAM pairs classic films with guest curators, including Questlove, Bryan Stevenson and John Turturro, and adds a free street party with local artists and vendors. Presented with Spike Lee and Clara Wu Tsai, it turns a screening series into a neighborhood event.

The lesson for brands and institutions: the free, open-door part of an event is often what builds the audience for everything else.
